notes: Indian furniture/home-decor Shopify store (orangetreehomes.myshopify.com). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (explicit 'Allow: /products/ /collections/ /pages/' blocks for anthropic-ai and Claude-Web); accessed via direct HTTP fetch of collections.json/products.json + rendered homepage/search HTML, no blocks encountered. Main nav (parsed from homepage HTML) is 100% product-type/furniture-line based (Sofas, Coffee Tables, Floor Lamps, Chandeliers, named furniture collections like Dastoori/Aether/Empire, etc.) — zero holiday/festival nav items, no Christmas anywhere on the site (internal search for 'christmas' returns 0 results; nonsense-slug search 'zzznonsense123' also returns 0, confirming the search engine is discriminating, not a default-results trap). Full collections.json enumeration (300 collections total, confirmed via limit=250 pagination through page 3 which returned 0) was grepped for the full seasonal vocabulary (Christmas/Xmas, Diwali/Deepavali, Halloween, Holi, Rakhi/Raksha Bandhan, Navratri, Dussehra, Eid, Ganesh Chaturthi, Janmashtami, Pongal, Onam, Durga Puja, Karwa Chauth, Sankranti, Baisakhi, Valentine, Easter, Thanksgiving, New Year, Mother's/Father's Day, Black Friday, Festive/Festival/Holiday). 9 handles matched and every one was individually sampled via /collections/<handle>/products.json (10-250 item samples) and product titles/tags inspected — all 9 failed the occasion-specific-content test and were excluded as false positives: (1) 'father-day-sale' (products_count 1656) and 'mothers-day-sale-products' (products_count 1666) are BYTE-IDENTICAL product lists (verified: first 250 product IDs in identical order) — the classic generic-catalog-reused-under-a-holiday-name pattern; combined with covering ~84-85% of the site's ~1969-product catalog (total confirmed via the 'all'/'all-products' collections), these are plainly a generic bulk marketing/sale collection, not real Mother's/Father's Day PLPs. (2) 'luxury-diwali-gift' (products_count 818, ~42% of the entire catalog, on par with the site's whole 'Furniture' (890) and 'Lighting' (812) top-level categories) — sampled 328 of 818 products; titles are generic lamps, wall decor, candle stands, coasters, cheese boards, cake stands with zero Diwali-specific vocabulary (no diya, toran, rangoli, pooja/puja thali, diwali hamper); the only keyword hits were the internal ops tag 'festive quick delivery' and sale tag 'Festive 40', not genuine occasion markers. (3) 'diwali-home-lighting' (products_count 119, 96 actually enumerable) — full list is plain floor/wall/hanging/table lamps and chandeliers (Klimt, Mallawi, Henka, Keshi, etc. lamp lines), identical in character to the generic 'lighting' collection (812 products); no diyas, string/fairy lights, or festive-lighting-specific items. (4) 'diwali-furniture-offer' (products_count 46) — products.json returns an EMPTY product list ({"products":[]}) on repeated fetch, i.e. a stale/broken collection with zero live products despite the (known-inflated) products_count field. (5) 'festive-exclusive-flat-40-off' (123) and 'festive-furniture-collection' (20) are discount/clearance collections (tags 'Bulk sell', 'Clearance Products', 'diwali sale', 'Festive 40') — pure sale/offer pages, excluded per rules §4 (Diwali Offers / Festive Offers). (6) 'quick-festive-delivery' (70) is an operational fast-shipping tag collection (wall lamps, side tables), not occasion content. (7) 'reflections-of-festivity' (23) is generic mirrors and wall decor with no Diwali-specific items. Internal search for 'diwali' (127 results) surfaces the same generic lamps/lanterns/coffee-table mix via the 'diwali sale' tag, not a dedicated Diwali PLP. No genuine Holi, Rakhi/Raksha Bandhan, Eid, Navratri, Dussehra, Valentine's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, New Year, or any other festival category exists in the taxonomy either (none of those terms appear in collection handles/titles or main nav at all; the few 'Holi Sale' hits found sitewide are all product discount/markdown tags, e.g. '10%'/'30SALE'/'Holi Sale' used as a generic sale-campaign label across unrelated furniture/lighting SKUs, not a Holi shopping category). Conclusion: this company sells home furniture/lighting/decor year-round and reuses seasonal names purely as marketing/sale-campaign labels on generic inventory; it has no genuine seasonal/holiday product-listing category satisfying the PLP + occasion-association + content-verification test. Recorded as NO_SEASONAL per rules §12/§18 after real investigation (nav, mega-menu equivalent, full collections.json enumeration, internal search with discrimination check, and content sampling of every holiday-named handle found).
